mainTopic: The sources for each tragedy that happened on תשעה באב, stories of the חורבן, and lessening joy in אב versus increasing it in אדר.
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: one idol 'tells' another that they are working together to destroy the בית המקדש. Then the גמרא goes through the משנה's list of tragedies on תשעה באב, giving a source for each one. For the decree against the מרגלים' generation, it counts days through the פסוקים from 20 אייר to 29 סיון, when the מרגלים were sent. אביי explains that תמוז had 30 days that year, so the 40 days ended on 8 אב and the people cried for nothing on the night of תשעה באב. ה׳ answered that this would become a crying for all generations. For the first בית המקדש, a ברייתא reconciles פסוקים that give the 7th and the 10th: the enemy entered on the 7th, the fire was set late on the 9th, and it burned through the 10th. רבי יוחנן would have fixed the fast on the 10th, but the רבנן prefer the beginning of the tragedy. The second חורבן is learned from the rule that bad events fall on a bad day, and ביתר is known by tradition. The plowing of the city leads to the story of the Roman officer who gave his life to save רבן גמליאל, followed by the young כהנים who returned the keys of the היכל to ה׳. The amud ends with the משנה's rule that joy is lessened from the start of אב, and רב's teaching that joy is increased from the start of אדר.

steps.title: The idol says: I am helping you destroy the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the idol placed in the היכל. It is as if one idol tells the other: you want to destroy the בית המקדש, and I am lending you a hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: You want to destroy the House (the Temple); I have given you my hand.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the earlier discussion about the צלם that was placed in the היכל. The גמרא pictures one idol 'speaking' to the other, saying they are partners in bringing destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that idol worship inside the בית המקדש was not a small sin. It actively 'worked together' to cause the חורבן. With this line the previous topic ends, and the גמרא is about to turn to a new line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I have handed over / given (as help)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the PREVIOUS topic, the צלם in the היכל. It is not connected to the מרגלים discussion that starts right after it.

phrases.english: You want to destroy the House (the Temple)
phrases.notes: As if one idol is speaking to the other.

phrases.english: I have given you a hand (to help you).
phrases.notes: Meaning: we are partners in causing the destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion (on the previous amud) of the idol placed in the היכל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Idol worship in the בית המקדש is pictured as actively joining forces to bring about its destruction.

steps.title: How do we know the decree against entering the land was on תשעה באב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that on תשעה באב it was decreed our ancestors would not enter the land. It then asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the Ninth of Av it was decreed upon our ancestors that they would not enter the land. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה and asking how we know the date. This is a setup line that prepares a long calendar proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה tells us about the sin of the מרגלים and the punishment, but it never openly says this happened on תשעה באב. So the גמרא needs to show, using the dates in the פסוקים, that the day of crying and punishment fell exactly on תשעה באב.

steps.title: Starting point: the משכן was set up on 1 ניסן of the second year
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins with the פסוק saying the משכן was put up on the first of ניסן in the second year. A teaching of 'מר' adds that in that second year משה also sent the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'It was in the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, the משכן was set up.' And the Master said: In the first year משה made the משכן; in the second year משה set up the משכן and sent spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building a timeline. It sets the starting point, the second year after leaving מצרים, and connects the sending of the מרגלים to that same year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote from 'מר' is the key link. It tells us the מרגלים were sent in the second year, the same year the משכן was set up. Now every date in the second year can be counted forward to find when the מרגלים left and returned.

keyTerms.meaning: and the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first anchor: the מרגלים were sent in the second year, the year that began with setting up the משכן on 1 ניסן.

steps.title: The cloud lifted on 20 אייר
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says that on the 20th of the second month (אייר) of the second year, the cloud lifted from the משכן, meaning the people began to travel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'It was in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud was lifted from upon the Tabernacle of Testimony.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the next date to the timeline. The people left הר סיני on 20 אייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives an exact day from which we can start counting. Every event that follows will be added on top of 20 אייר until we reach the sending of the מרגלים.

steps.title: Three days of travel, and turning away from ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The people traveled three days from הר סיני. רבי חמא בר חנינא adds that on that very day they turned away from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'They traveled from the mountain of ה׳ a three-day journey.' רבי חמא בר חנינא said: On that day they turned away from following ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds three more days to the count, bringing us to 23 אייר. Along the way it quotes רבי חמא בר חנינא about the people's attitude when they left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the calendar, what matters is the 'three days.' רבי חמא בר חנינא's comment is a side point. It shows the spiritual decline had already started as they left סיני.

steps.title: A month of eating meat brings us to 22 סיון
steps.stepSummary: The people complained and wanted meat, and ה׳ gave them meat 'for a month of days.' Adding a month to 23 אייר brings us to 22 סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'The mixed crowd among them had a strong craving, and the Children of Israel also cried again...' And it is written: 'Until a month of days...' So we reach the twenty-second of סיון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the month when the people ate the meat. That moves the timeline to 22 סיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The episode of the craving for meat lasted a full month, according to the פסוק. Counting a month from 23 אייר lands on 22 סיון. The count is getting closer to the day the מרגלים were sent.

steps.title: מרים's seven days bring us to 29 סיון, when the spies were sent
steps.stepSummary: מרים was shut out of the camp for 7 days, bringing us to 29 סיון. Right after that, the תורה says 'שלח לך אנשים,' so the מרגלים were sent on 29 סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'מרים was shut out for seven days.' So we reach the twenty-ninth of סיון. And it is written: 'Send for yourself men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the 7 days of מרים's צרעת and arrives at 29 סיון. That is the day the מרגלים were sent out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרשה of the מרגלים comes right after the story of מרים. So the sending happened on 29 סיון. Next the גמרא will add the 40 days of spying to reach the night of crying on תשעה באב.
steps.whatToRemember: The full count so far: 20 אייר (cloud lifts) → +3 days → +a month of meat = 22 סיון → +7 days of מרים = 29 סיון, when the מרגלים were sent. The proof is not finished yet. The 40 days of spying still need to be added.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And Miriam was shut out for seven days'
phrases.notes: במדבר יב:טו. The people waited for her.

phrases.english: which comes out to the twenty-ninth of Sivan.
phrases.notes: 22 סיון + 7 = 29 סיון.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Send for yourself men.'

steps.whyThisMatters: Once we know the מרגלים left on 29 סיון, adding their 40 days will bring us to the night of crying, which is the day of the decree on תשעה באב.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the date, and the spies return after forty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that the מרגלים were sent on 29 סיון. A פסוק adds that they came back after 40 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: on the 29th of סיון משה sent the spies. And the פסוק says: 'They returned from scouting the land at the end of forty days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what we figured out ourselves: the מרגלים were sent on 29 סיון. Then it quotes the פסוק saying they were gone for 40 days, so we can count forward to their return date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3-7 reached 29 סיון by counting through the פסוקים. Now a ברייתא backs up that result. The 40-day trip is the next piece we need, because counting 40 days from 29 סיון should land us on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה)
The spies משה sent to scout ארץ ישראל
At the end of forty days

Moshe sent the spies,

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And they returned from scouting the land'
at the end of forty days.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְּסִיוָן שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה מְרַגְּלִים

steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, and the פסוק in במדבר יג:כה

steps.title: The count comes out one day short
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that counting from 29 סיון to תשעה באב gives only 39 days, not 40.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are forty days minus one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math and finds a problem. From 29 סיון through 8 אב, the day before the night of crying, is only 39 days, not the 40 the פסוק says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the count. סיון has 30 days, so 29 and 30 סיון give 2 days. A regular 29-day תמוז gives 29 more. Then 1-8 אב gives 8 more. That totals 39 days. The spies returned during the day and the people cried that night (step 11), so the 40 days must end on 8 אב for the crying to fall on the night of 9 אב. With only 39 days, the 40th day would be 9 אב, and the crying would fall on the night of the 10th.

keyTerms.meaning: They are / they come out to

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם נְכֵי חַד הָווּ!
phrases.english: These are forty days minus one!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם נְכֵי חַד הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the calculation built in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 40 days after 29 סיון brings us to תשעה באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a 30-day סיון and a normal 29-day תמוז, 29 סיון through 8 אב is only 39 days. A full 40 days would end on 9 אב, which pushes the night of crying to the night of 10 אב.

steps.title: אביי says תמוז was a full month that year
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that in that year תמוז had 30 days. That extra day brings the count to exactly 40.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The month of תמוז in that year was made full, as the פסוק says: 'He called an appointed time against me to crush my young men.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי solves the missing day by saying תמוז had 30 days that year instead of 29. He brings a hint from מגילת איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Months can have 29 or 30 days, depending on when ראש חודש is set. If תמוז had 30 days, the count gains one day and lands exactly on תשעה באב. The פסוק 'קרא עלי מועד' is read as saying an 'appointed time' (an extra day for ראש חודש) was set against us, so that the disaster would fall on that exact day.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it full, meaning a 30-day month
Appointed time, here hinting at the setting of ראש חודש

phrases.english: Abaye said: Tammuz of that year,
they made it full (30 days),
as it is written: 'He called an appointed time against me'
to crush my young men.'
phrases.notes: איכה א:טו

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּמּוּז דְּהַהִיא שַׁתָּא מַלּוֹיֵי מַלְּיוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the one-day-short problem raised in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed תמוז had its usual 29 days, which leaves the count one day short.
steps.terutzMaskana: That year תמוז had 30 days, so the 40 days ended on 8 אב, and the crying that followed fell on the night of תשעה באב.

steps.title: The night of crying was תשעה באב, so it became a day of crying for all generations
steps.stepSummary: The people cried the night the spies returned. רבי יוחנן teaches that this was the night of תשעה באב, and ה׳ made it a day of real crying for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק says: 'The whole congregation raised their voice, and the people cried that night.' רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That night was the night of תשעה באב‎. ה׳ said to them: You cried a crying for nothing, and I will set for you a crying for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The night the people cried over the spies' report was תשעה באב‎. ה׳ then made that date a day of real tragedy forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the 40 days end on 8 אב, the night that follows, when the people cried 'that night,' is the night of תשעה באב. The key idea is measure for measure: they cried over nothing, so ה׳ gave them something real to cry about on that same day. This explains why so many later disasters fall on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: The night of the Ninth of אב
Crying for nothing, with no real reason

steps.whatToRemember: The decree that the generation of the מדבר would not enter ארץ ישראל came on תשעה באב, because the people cried over nothing that night. ה׳ made it a permanent day of crying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the root of why תשעה באב is a day of mourning. It explains why later tragedies, like the destruction of the בית המקדש, also came on this date.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The decree against the generation of the מדבר happened on תשעה באב, the first of the tragedies listed in the משנה.

steps.title: The first בית המקדש was destroyed: a פסוק says the 7th of the fifth month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next tragedy in the משנה, the destruction of the first בית המקדש. It quotes a פסוק in מלכים that dates נבוזראדן's arrival to the 7th of the fifth month (אב).
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית המקדש was destroyed the first time, as the פסוק says: 'In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month, in the nineteenth year of King נבוכדנצר, king of Babylon, נבוזראדן, chief of the guards, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem, and he burned the house of ה׳...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה: the first בית המקדש was destroyed on תשעה באב. It brings a פסוק from מלכים, but that פסוק mentions the 7th of אב, not the 9th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fifth month, counting from ניסן, is אב, so the month fits. But the date given is the 7th, which does not match תשעה באב. This sets up the next step, where a second פסוק gives yet another date.

steps.title: A second פסוק says the 10th of the month instead
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק, in ירמיהו, describes the same event but dates it to the 10th of the fifth month. This creates an implied contradiction with the 7th.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another פסוק says: 'In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, in the nineteenth year of King נבוכדנצר, king of Babylon, נבוזראדן, chief of the guards, who stood before the king of Babylon, came into Jerusalem...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a problem by placing a second פסוק next to the first. One says the 7th, the other says the 10th, and neither says the 9th. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים describe the same event with different dates. The גמרא does not spell out the question yet, but putting them side by side raises it. How can both be true, and how do we get תשעה באב from them? Expect a ברייתא to explain how all three dates fit together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places a second, conflicting date next to the פסוק in step 12, setting up a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The dating of the destruction of the first בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in מלכים says the 7th and the פסוק in ירמיהו says the 10th. They cannot both be the single date, and neither is the 9th.

steps.title: Both dates are true: the enemy entered on the 7th
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא resolves the contradiction between the 7th and the 10th. On the 7th the enemy entered the היכל, and on the 7th and 8th they ate there and defiled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: You can't say it happened on the 7th, because a פסוק already says 'on the 10th.' And you can't say it happened on the 10th, because a פסוק already says 'on the 7th.' So how does it work? On the 7th the non-Jews entered the היכל, and on the 7th and the 8th they ate there and defiled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the contradiction from the last step. Both dates are correct because they describe different stages of the same event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first admits that neither פסוק can simply be ignored. It then begins splitting the event into stages. The 7th is when the enemy entered the היכל, and on the 7th and 8th they defiled it. The 10th will be explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים that is outside the משנה)
So how does it work? (introduces a way to reconcile sources)
The Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The 7th is NOT the day of the burning. The 7th is when the enemy entered. The fire came later.

phrases.english: And it is taught in a baraita: It is impossible to say 'on the seventh,'
since it has already been stated 'on the tenth.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק in ירמיהו

phrases.english: And it is impossible to say 'on the tenth,'
since it has already been stated 'on the seventh.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק in מלכים

phrases.english: So how is this to be understood?
On the seventh, gentiles entered the Sanctuary,
and they ate and defiled it on the seventh and the eighth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the event into stages, so each פסוק describes a different stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give two different dates for one event.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 7th marks the enemy's entry. The later burning will explain the 10th.

steps.title: The fire began late on the 9th and burned through the 10th
steps.stepSummary: On the 9th, close to nightfall, the enemy set the היכל on fire, and it burned all through the next day. A פסוק about the evening shadows supports this timing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on the 9th, close to nightfall, they set it on fire, and it kept burning the whole day. As the פסוק says: 'Woe to us, for the day has turned, for the evening shadows are stretching out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its timeline. The fire started at the very end of the 9th and burned through the 10th, which explains the date in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the answer: the 7th is the entry, and the 10th is the day the היכל was mostly burning. The פסוק in ירמיהו about the day 'turning' toward evening is read as a hint that the fire began as the day was ending.

phrases.english: And on the ninth, close to nightfall,
they set fire to it,
and it kept on burning
the entire day.
As it is stated: 'Woe unto us, for the day has declined,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ו:ד

phrases.english: 'for the shadows of the evening are stretched out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְשִׁיעִי סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁיכָה הֵצִיתוּ בּוֹ אֶת הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's timeline begun in Step 14 and brings a פסוק as support
steps.raayaObject: That the fire began at the end of the 9th and continued into the 10th
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 6:4: 'Woe unto us, for the day has declined, for the shadows of the evening are stretched out'
steps.whatToRemember: 7th: the enemy entered. 7th and 8th: they defiled the היכל. Late on the 9th: the fire was set. The 10th: it burned. So both פסוקים are true.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן would have set the fast on the 10th
steps.stepSummary: Because most of the היכל burned on the 10th, רבי יוחנן says that if he had lived then, he would have set the fast on the 10th.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said: If I had lived in that generation, I would have set the fast only on the 10th, because most of the היכל was burned on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the ברייתא's timeline to a known statement of רבי יוחנן. His opinion makes sense now that we know most of the burning happened on the 10th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'וְהַיְינוּ' shows that the ברייתא explains why רבי יוחנן said this. Since the bulk of the destruction was on the 10th, he feels the fast belongs there. This sets up the question of why the רבנן chose the 9th.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] meant when he said
I would have established it (the fast)

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yochanan meant when he said:
Had I been in that generation,
I would have established it only on the tenth,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרוּבּוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל בּוֹ נִשְׂרַף.
phrases.english: because most of the Sanctuary was burned on that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the timeline from Steps 14-15 to explain רבי יוחנן's opinion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן holds the fast should mark the day when most of the destruction happened, which is the 10th of אב.

steps.title: The רבנן prefer to mark the beginning of the tragedy
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן set the fast on the 9th because the start of a disaster is the more important moment to mark.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They hold that the beginning of the tragedy is more important.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן did not follow רבי יוחנן's logic. They chose the 9th, when the fire started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an unspoken question: if most of the היכל burned on the 10th, why is the fast on the 9th? The answer is that the רבנן look at when the disaster began, not when most of the damage happened. Both sides agree on the facts and differ only on which moment to mark.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages? (asks how they would respond)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we fast on תשעה באב and not on the 10th. The halacha follows the רבנן.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis (why did they choose the ninth)?
The beginning of the calamity is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן's choice of the 9th against רבי יוחנן's reasoning
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different principle for choosing the date
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fast should be on the day when most of the היכל burned (the 10th).
steps.terutzMaskana: The fast marks the beginning of the disaster (the 9th).

steps.title: How do we know the second בית המקדש was destroyed on the 9th?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and asks for the source that the second חורבן was also on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding the second destruction, how do we know it was on the 9th of אב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the next tragedy listed in the משנה, the destruction of the second בית המקדש. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first בית המקדש, פסוקים gave the date. There are no פסוקים in תנ"ך about the second חורבן, so the גמרא needs a different kind of source.

keyTerms.meaning: The second time (the destruction of the second בית המקדש)

phrases.english: And for the second time, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first-חורבן discussion and moves to the next tragedy in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the second בית המקדש was destroyed on תשעה באב

steps.title: Good comes on good days, bad on bad days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ה׳ brings good events on a day that is already good and bad events on a day that is already bad. So the second חורבן was also on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Good things are brought about on a good day, and bad things on a bad day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a general principle. Since תשעה באב was already a day of tragedy, the second destruction was also steered to that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a pattern rule, not a date in a פסוק. Since the spies and the first חורבן already made תשעה באב a 'guilty' day, more disasters were drawn to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring about / steer (events toward a certain day)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Merit is brought about on a meritorious day,
and guilt on a guilty day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle that bad events gather on an already-bad day explains why the second חורבן fell on תשעה באב.

steps.title: The first חורבן fell on a day full of signs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the details of the day of the first חורבן. It was תשעה באב, מוצאי שבת, the year after שמיטה, and the week of the משמר of יהויריב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When the בית המקדש was destroyed the first time, that day was תשעה באב. It was מוצאי שבת. It was the year after שמיטה. And it was the week of the משמר of יהויריב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and describes the exact day of the first destruction. It is building a picture that the second destruction will match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many 'bad' details all landed on one day. This illustrates the rule of the previous step and prepares the claim that the second חורבן matched it.

keyTerms.meaning: The year right after the שמיטה year
The weekly priestly shift (משמר) of the family יהויריב

phrases.english: They said: When the Temple was destroyed the first time,
that day was the Ninth of Av,
and it was the conclusion of Shabbat,
and it was the year after the Sabbatical Year,
and it was the priestly watch of Yehoyariv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the 'bad day' principle from Step 19
steps.raayaObject: That the destruction gathered on a day marked by many ill-fated details

steps.title: The לויים were cut off mid-song, and the same happened at the second חורבן
steps.stepSummary: The לויים were singing a פסוק about ה׳ punishing the wicked and were conquered before they could finish it. The same thing happened at the second חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לויים were singing their song, standing on their platform. Which song were they singing? 'He turned their wickedness back on them, and He will destroy them through their own evil.' They didn't manage to say 'ה׳ our God will destroy them' before the non-Jews came and conquered them. And the same happened at the second destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its description of the first חורבן. It then ends with 'וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה', which answers our question: the second destruction happened the same way, on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail of the song being cut off shows how sudden the attack was. The key words for our question are 'וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.' They tell us the second חורבן matched the first, including the date of תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Levites, who sang in the בית המקדש
Their platform (where the Levites stood to sing)
He will cut them off / destroy them
And so too at the second destruction

steps.whatToRemember: First בית המקדש: proven from פסוקים (entered on the 7th, burned late on the 9th into the 10th, fast on the 9th per the רבנן). Second בית המקדש: proven from the ברייתא's rule that bad events fall on a bad day, ending with 'וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.'
steps.confusionAlert: 'וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה' is short, but it is the actual answer to 'וּבַשְּׁנִיָּה מְנָלַן.' Don't treat it as an extra detail.

phrases.english: And the Levites were reciting song,
and standing on their platform.
And what song were they reciting?
'And He brought back upon them their iniquity,'
phrases.notes: תהלים צד:כג

phrases.english: 'and in their evil He will cut them off.'
And they did not manage to say
'The Lord our God will cut them off,'
before gentiles came and conquered them.
And so too at the second destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's description and applies it to the second חורבן, closing the question of Step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second בית המקדש was destroyed on תשעה באב just like the first, because tragedy is drawn to an already tragic day.

steps.title: ביתר's fall is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that the capture of ביתר on תשעה באב has no פסוק source. It is known through a received tradition (גמרא).
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said ביתר was captured on תשעה באב. How do we know? By tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the fall of ביתר. It answers in one word that this is a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the earlier items the גמרא looked for a source in a פסוק or a ברייתא. Here it says there is no written source; the date was handed down from teacher to student. Here the word גמרא means 'received tradition', not 'the Talmud'.

keyTerms.meaning: Beitar, the last fortress of the בר כוכבא revolt

steps.confusionAlert: The word גמרא here does not mean the Talmud. It means 'we have this as a tradition.'

phrases.english: [The משנה said] Beitar was captured [on תשעה באב] —
This is known by tradition.
phrases.notes: No פסוק is brought. The date was passed down orally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the second חורבן to the next item in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fall of ביתר on תשעה באב is known by received tradition.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the plowing of the Temple
steps.stepSummary: For the משנה's line 'the city was plowed', the גמרא brings a ברייתא. It says that when טורנוסרופוס plowed the היכל, a death decree was issued against רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'the city was plowed', a ברייתא teaches: when the wicked טורנוסרופוס plowed the היכל, a decree was made that רבן גמליאל should be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last item in the משנה, the plowing of the city, and supports it with a ברייתא. This also sets up a story about רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that the plowing really happened, carried out by the Roman governor טורנוסרופוס. It then adds a second evil decree from that same time, the order to kill רבן גמליאל. The rest of the story grows out of this decree.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
Turnus Rufus, the Roman governor of Judea

phrases.english: [The משנה said] the city was plowed — it is taught in a ברייתא:
When the wicked Turnus Rufus plowed the Sanctuary,

phrases.aramaic: נִגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַהֲרִיגָה.
phrases.english: a decree was issued against Rabban Gamliel, to execute him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next and last item in the משנה's list.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's statement that the city was plowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing טורנוסרופוס plowing the היכל

steps.title: The officer's hidden warning and רבן גמליאל's escape
steps.stepSummary: A Roman officer came into the בית המדרש and called out a coded hint: 'the man with the nose is wanted.' רבן גמליאל understood and went into hiding.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain officer came, stood in the study hall and said, 'The man with the nose is wanted! The man with the nose is wanted!' רבן גמליאל heard this and went to hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins. A Roman officer quietly warns רבן גמליאל, who escapes into hiding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The man with the nose' was a hint to the most prominent person, who stands out the way a nose stands out on a face. The officer did not name רבן גמליאל openly, so he could warn him without betraying himself. The hint worked, and רבן גמליאל hid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the man with the nose', a hint to the leading person

phrases.aramaic: בָּא אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן וְעָמַד בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: A certain officer came and stood in the study hall,
and said: The man with the nose is wanted,
phrases.notes: A hidden hint to רבן גמליאל, the most prominent man of his generation.

phrases.english: the man with the nose is wanted.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אֲזַל טְשָׁא מִינַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel heard, and went and hid from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן וְעָמַד בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened after the decree against רבן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Roman officer secretly warned רבן גמליאל, who went into hiding.

steps.title: The officer's deal and רבן גמליאל's oath
steps.stepSummary: The officer secretly asked רבן גמליאל: if I save you, will you bring me to עולם הבא? רבן גמליאל said yes and swore to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The officer went to him privately and said: 'If I save you, will you bring me into the World to Come?' He answered, 'Yes.' The officer said, 'Swear to me.' He swore to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The officer offers to save רבן גמליאל in exchange for a place in עולם הבא, and רבן גמליאל swears to it. This sets up the officer's sacrifice in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer is willing to pay a huge price, but he wants a guarantee first. He asks for an oath, not only a promise, to be sure the deal is real.

phrases.english: The officer went to him in private
and said to him: If I save you,
will you bring me to the World to Come?
He said to him: Yes.
The officer said to him: Swear to me.
He swore to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the officer now speaks to רבן גמליאל directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל swore that the officer would reach עולם הבא if he saved him.

steps.title: The officer gives his life to cancel the decree
steps.stepSummary: The officer went up to the roof, threw himself off and died. The Romans had a rule that if one of them died after they made a decree, they cancelled it, so רבן גמליאל was saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went up to the roof, fell, and died. We have a tradition that when the Romans made a decree and one of them died, they would cancel their decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The officer keeps his side of the deal by dying, and the גמרא explains why his death saved רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His death on its own would mean nothing unless we know the Roman custom. The Romans took the death of one of their own as a bad sign and cancelled the decree. So the officer's death was a planned way to cancel the order to kill רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: He went up to the roof, fell, and died.
And there is a tradition that when they issued a decree
and one of them died,
they would cancel their decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the deal made in the previous step and explains how it worked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The officer's death cancelled the Roman decree and saved רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice confirms the officer's reward
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול announced that the officer was destined for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Heavenly voice came out and said: That officer is destined for life in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Heaven itself confirms that the officer earned his reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer had asked רבן גמליאל for a promise, but the final word comes from Heaven. The בת קול shows that his act of self-sacrifice was truly accepted.
steps.whatToRemember: A non-Jewish Roman officer gave his life to save רבן גמליאל, and a בת קול declared that he would have עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A Heavenly voice emerged and said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן מְזוּמָּן לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: That officer is destined for the life of the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with Heaven's confirmation of the officer's reward.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The officer's self-sacrifice earned him a place in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The young priests return the keys to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: at the first חורבן, groups of young כהנים went up to the roof of the היכל with its keys. They said that since they had not been faithful guardians, the keys should be handed back to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: When the בית המקדש was destroyed the first time, groups and groups of young כהנים gathered with the keys of the היכל in their hands. They went up to the roof of the היכל and said before Him: 'Master of the World! Since we did not merit to be faithful treasurers, let the keys be handed over to You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the first חורבן. It describes how the young כהנים reacted as the בית המקדש was burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young כהנים admit that they failed to guard the בית המקדש properly. Instead of handing the keys to the enemy, they give them back to ה׳, the true Owner.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: When the Temple was destroyed the first time,

phrases.aramaic: נִתְקַבְּצוּ כִּיתּוֹת כִּיתּוֹת שֶׁל פִּרְחֵי כְּהוּנָּה
phrases.english: many groups of young priests gathered
with the keys of the Sanctuary in their hands,
and they went up to the roof of the Sanctuary,
and said before Him: Master of the World!

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְלָא זָכִינוּ לִהְיוֹת גִּזְבָּרִין נֶאֱמָנִים —
phrases.english: Since we did not merit to be faithful treasurers —
let the keys be handed over to You.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא that returns to the first חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young כהנים gave the keys of the היכל back to ה׳, admitting they had failed as its guardians.

steps.title: A hand from Heaven takes the keys
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים threw the keys upward, and something like the palm of a hand came out and took them. The כהנים then jumped into the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: They threw the keys upward. Something like the palm of a hand came out and took the keys from them. And they jumped and fell into the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Heaven accepts the keys, and the young כהנים die together with the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hand that takes the keys shows that ה׳ accepted them; the בית המקדש is now in His keeping. The כהנים jumping into the fire shows they could not bear to live on without it.
steps.whatToRemember: At the first חורבן the young כהנים returned the keys of the היכל to ה׳, a hand from Heaven took them, and the כהנים jumped into the fire.

phrases.english: And they threw them upward.
And something like the palm of a hand came out
and received them from them.
And they jumped and fell into the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the keys.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Heaven accepted the keys, and the young כהנים died along with the בית המקדש.

steps.title: ישעיהו's lament describes the young כהנים on the roofs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that ישעיהו הנביא lamented over the young כהנים who went up to the roofs and died. They did not die by the sword or in battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about them, ישעיהו the prophet lamented: 'The burden of the Valley of Vision. What is wrong with you, that you have all gone up to the roofs? You were full of noise, a loud city, a happy town. Your dead were not killed by the sword, and they did not die in war.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ישעיהו and reads it as a lament about the young כהנים from the previous story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details in the פסוק match the story. 'You have all gone up to the roofs' fits the כהנים who climbed onto the roof of the היכל. 'Your dead were not killed by the sword' fits the fact that they jumped into the fire instead of being killed by enemies. So the פסוק gives the story a source and shows it was mourned by a נביא.

keyTerms.meaning: the Valley of Vision, a name for ירושלים

phrases.english: And about them Isaiah the prophet lamented:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the young priests from the previous step.

phrases.english: 'The burden of the Valley of Vision'
What is wrong with you now
that you have all gone up to the roofs?
phrases.notes: This matches the priests who climbed onto the roof of the Sanctuary.

phrases.english: Full of noise, a loud city
a happy town
your dead were not killed by the sword
and did not die in war.'
phrases.notes: They died by jumping into the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק that matches the story of the כהנים in steps 28-29.
steps.raayaObject: The story of the young כהנים who went up to the roof and died in the fire.

steps.title: Even ה׳ cries over the destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a פסוק showing that even הקדוש ברוך הוא shouts and cries over the חורבן. This closes the series of stories.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even about הקדוש ברוך הוא it says: 'Shouting over walls, and crying out to the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the חורבן stories by saying that not only people mourned. ה׳ Himself cries over the destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (even) moves the lament up a level. First a נביא mourned, and now ה׳ is described as shouting and crying out to the mountain, meaning הר הבית. This gives a powerful ending to the stories before the גמרא returns to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: shouting over walls (also read as breaking down walls)

steps.whatToRemember: The stories of the חורבן end with the idea that ה׳ Himself mourns the destruction of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Even about the Holy One, Blessed be He, it is said:
'Shouting over walls, and crying out to the mountain.'
phrases.notes: From ישעיהו כב:ה, the same chapter as the previous פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the lament from step 30 and lifts it from the נביא to ה׳ Himself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The mourning over the חורבן reaches all the way to הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: from the start of אב we lessen joy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next line: once אב begins, we reduce שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From when אב begins, we lessen joy,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The stories are finished, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה by quoting its next rule. This is a setup line that opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וכו׳' (and so on) show that only the opening words of the משנה line are quoted. Quoting the משנה tells us that the next statements explain or add to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: from when the month of אב begins
and so on (the quote continues in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule being made here. It is a quote of the משנה that opens a new section after the long stories.

phrases.english: From when Av begins
we lessen joy, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the beginning of אב, we lessen שמחה.

steps.title: Just as joy is lessened in אב, joy is increased in אדר
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches the opposite side of the משנה: just as we lessen שמחה from the start of אב, we increase שמחה from the start of אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, the son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: Just as we lessen joy from when אב begins, so too we increase joy from when אדר begins.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a matching rule to the משנה. אב is a time to lessen joy, and אדר is a time to increase joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כשם... כך' (just as... so too) sets up a direct comparison. In אב sad events happened, so the whole month starts with less joy. In אדר the miracle of פורים happened, so the whole month starts with more joy. The משנה only taught the sad side, and רב adds the happy side.

keyTerms.meaning: the month of אדר, when פורים happens

steps.whatToRemember: משנכנס אב ממעטין בשמחה, and משנכנס אדר מרבין בשמחה. The whole month takes on the feeling of its main event.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the source of the well-known practice of increasing שמחה throughout the month of אדר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
Just as from when Av begins
we lessen joy
so too from when Adar begins
we increase joy.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אָב מְמַעֲטִין בְּשִׂמְחָה כָּךְ מִשֶּׁנִּכְנַס אֲדָר מַרְבִּין בְּשִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a matching opposite rule to the משנה quoted in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the start of אדר, we increase שמחה, the mirror image of lessening שמחה in אב.
